newsitem.title: GERMANY: German prosecutors accuse Iran of state terrorism.
newsitem.headline: German prosecutors accuse Iran of state terrorism.

text.p: German prosecutors on Friday renewed accusations of "state terrorism" against Iran for allegedly ordering the killing of four Kurdish-Iranian opposition members.
State prosecutor Bruno Jost also accused Iran of trying to discredit a key witness in the trial of one Iranian and four Lebanese accused of murdering the dissidents in a Berlin restaurant in 1992.

Iran was angered when prosecutors made similar accusations in an earlier summing-up, and when the German Federal Prosecutor issued an arrest warrant last year against Tehran's Intelligence Minister Ali Fallahiyan in connection with the assassinations.

Bonn has been at pains to assure Iran that its judiciary is independent and that the trial is not political. But relations were strained even further when former Iranian president Abolhassan Banisadr testified late last year that top Iranian government leaders approved the killings.

Banisadr persuaded several other opponents of the Tehran government to testify. Prosecutor Jost said Iran had attempted to discredit one of these witnesses with an "assortment of half-truths, slanders, lies and false accusations".
Iran denies any involvement in the assassinations and says they were the result of infighting within the Kurdish opposition.
